PullRequest.Title: Add HydraFusion Max to Auto's tiers
PullRequest.Body:
Adds HydraFusion Max after HydraFusion in Auto's "Optimize for" tiers. It is only offered when HydraFusion v2 is enabled, and the two HydraFusion options sit on a row of their own.

Also addresses https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340820#discussion_r4235325411: Auto's discount description now updates with the clicked tier instead of waiting for the save to re-render.

Note: telemetry reports Max turns as `modelSelectionKind: 'hydrafusionMax'`.

**Test:** set `"chat.copilot.hydraFusion.enabled": "v2"`, then open Auto's details in an Agent Host Copilot chat.

cc: @lramos15

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, search, refresh, and inspect Auto in the tabbed model picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The UI synchronously filters the already-loaded model array, builds destinations and rows, constructs Auto's card, and lays out the segmented radio. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is on this rendering path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The loaded model count controls list scans; the new HydraFusion lookup checks exactly two known IDs. The rendered change adds at most one extra model option, one row break, and one hidden description.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded UI work; refreshes are synchronous and no new queue, limiter, or parallel operation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model cards are cached while the picker remains visible and disposed when it closes. HydraFusion discovery is recomputed from the in-memory model list, but the candidate key set is fixed at two; no cold/warm external cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the changed helpers and all picker call sites were traced; they operate only on in-memory arrays and DOM nodes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installations can expose different model counts, but the additional work is a small constant number of linear scans during explicit picker rendering rather than per frame or per keystroke filtering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra synchronous work is bounded and small, and no expensive boundary or unbounded retained state was added.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose HydraFusion Max or another Auto optimization tier
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A deliberate activation updates the radio and description immediately, invokes the existing model-selection callback, and the agent's established model-change path may update the SDK session and persisted session metadata. The immediate description render is tiny and occurs once per activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update the Copilot SDK session's selected model via entry.setModel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one SDK model update for each accepted user model selection, serialized per chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selecting any existing model already used the same single setModel call; the diff only makes HydraFusion Max another valid choice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the existing model-selection boundary used for every model; it prepares the session for subsequent turns rather than being newly added to picker rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist session model metadata through _storeSessionMetadata when the session-scoped resource is selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one persistence operation per accepted session-scoped model selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same metadata persistence occurred for other model selections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It is awaited by the established model-change operation, but the PR does not increase calls per selection or move persistence onto a hotter path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected option per user activation; rapid activations are sequenced by the existing model-change path and do not fan out across models or sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing per-chat sequencer serializes model changes. The PR adds no aggregate parallelism or missing coalescing mechanism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The description replaces its prior DOM node and swaps its DisposableStore, disposing prior listeners. A same-tier render reuses the existing node; there is no accumulating cache or retained history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the picker callback was followed through _applyModelSelection to the existing sequenced agent model-change path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact SDK and storage latency varies, but cardinality and placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Max reuses the one-selection/one-update path, and the new immediate DOM update disposes replaced resources.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore an Agent Host chat and reconstruct completed Fusion turn history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session and chat subscriptions hydrate first, then turnsToHistory synchronously converts each turn. The changed turnToResponseDetails performs one response-part scan to recover the routed Fusion model before the existing conversion loop processes the same parts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate the existing session and chat state subscriptions from the Agent Host connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session subscription and one chat subscription for the restored chat, independent of turn or response-part count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscriptions hydrated before turnsToHistory; the diff changes only in-memory labeling after hydration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Hydration must finish before history conversion, as before; the changed response-label scan happens afterward and adds no IPC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total completed turns and total response parts across the restored chat. The added work is O(total response parts), with metadata parsing only for system-notification parts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: History conversion is synchronous after subscription hydration and runs once when providing session content; history is explicitly built once rather than on every live update.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold restore hydrates subscriptions and builds history once. An already-open session retains the built history and does not repeatedly run this conversion; no new cache or negative-cache state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: callers show completed history is built once, and the completion path calls the helper only once for the completed turn rather than on each streaming update.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Chats can vary substantially in response-part count, but the added pass preserves linear scaling and is lightweight relative to the existing mandatory per-part reconstruction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Although the diff replaces a short-circuit predicate with a full scan, it runs once per restored/completed turn and does not change asymptotic scaling or add an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh the Copilot model catalog and process Fusion progress/telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing model-list request completes, _publishModels adds up to two synthetic HydraFusion entries in memory, and incoming Fusion events attach a short model ID to milestone metadata and telemetry classification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the Copilot model catalog through _listModels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per existing refresh attempt, with the pre-existing bounded retry policy; synthetic HydraFusion insertion does not issue another request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model-list request and retries ran before publication; previously publication could append one HydraFusion entry instead of up to two.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The catalog request already precedes model publication. The diff only performs bounded in-memory insertion after it resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive and persist existing Agent Host Fusion progress events containing system-notification metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata field is added to each existing Fusion milestone event; no additional event is emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same milestone events were emitted without the fusionModel field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The event already crosses the Agent Host boundary; the diff adds a short string to the existing payload without adding round trips or blocking work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The CAPI model count for publication and the number of Fusion milestones in one turn. The synthetic model set is fixed at two and retained progress state adds only one current model string per CopilotFusionProgress instance.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing model refresh/retry machinery controls the single catalog request. Fusion events are processed sequentially; no new requests, tasks, or concurrent burst is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Published models replace the observable array on each existing refresh. _syntheticModel is cleared on reset, while per-milestone metadata lives only with its corresponding response part; no unbounded key set or cache was introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: publication and event handling were traced to their existing request/event boundaries and reset lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size and milestone count vary, but the changed cardinality is fixed or proportional only to already-existing events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Network/IPC counts and retry/concurrency behavior are unchanged, while added allocations and retention are tightly bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 33 changed files. Traced model-picker rendering and selection, model publication, Fusion event metadata, telemetry, and session-history reconstruction. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; all changed work is bounded, preserves existing boundary cardinality, and has explicit disposal/reset ownership.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
